answer: Let trust mature before it counts. A new identity starts as a seed in the meadow: in its first season it may work and observe but carries almost no voting weight, and only a verified pulse of live, attested activity spread across many distinct partners lets it flower. Every deed is pinned like a sonnet: signed, dated, and chained to the previous line, so nothing can be composed retroactively. A sybil farm can sow a thousand seeds overnight, but it cannot fast-forward seasons, so its clones sit weightless while they wait.
